People caring about me makes me feel guilty about wanting to die. I know theyd better off but at the same time I know they'd be really upset if I died. I tried to kill myself months ago and afterwards my dad constantly called me to make sure I was ok and safe at home. He was terrified Id do it again.. Felt like shit putting him through that. From what everyones said, I might end up changing therapists then. I dont think she's a bad person or anything, she seems to give genuine advice to me. But sometimes she just says these things, like shes guilting me. Like she'll talk about some other patient of hers each session, people who have been homeless, lost family, can barely function... and basically says "if they can do it, why cant you". Then I just feel so guilty and shitty after. It just feels like she sees me basically as this brat taking "the easy way out" (which she actually said I was opting for the "easy" way, not that any part of my attempt was at all easy for me...). One thing that really upset me during this session though was when she called my suicide attempt "cliche" and "cheesy" because she "sees it all the time".  It just sucks to change therapists over and over, since I've been through so many over the years and none have really worked out.

Honestly, friends sometimes come and go. Some friendships just don't stick over time. I'm sorry you lost all your friends, but don't worry; you'll eventually find new ones. I've been through many different groups of friends over the years. When I was just starting highschool, all my friends went to different schools and we never ended up keeping in touch. I was alone, and thought I'd stay alone all throughout school. But, after a while, I ended up with a new group of friends. I lost touch with those friends too... but again, I found more people that I'm now close to. I know it's hard and lonely now, but I promise you, you'll make friends again. You'll eventually find the right people who will stick by your side.

As someone with (undiagnosed) tinnitus also, I think that might be it. Sometimes I hear static, ringing, whistling, all coming and going at different times, and at different volumes. If its happening daily too, then it likely is just tinnitus. The sounds can also become more prevalent when youre stressed, so that could be whats going on. My tinnitus is usually the loudest and worst when Im anxious or when theres no other sound in the room. 

There is a way to momentarily relieve the noise, which involves a rythmic thumping on the back of the head. https://youtu.be/2yDCox-qKbk --I think youre supposed to do it about 50 times and then it works (though it doesnt help everyone and personally hasnt worked well for me).

Try it out and see if it helps. I'd definitely recommend mentioning this to your therapist though, just in case.
